sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ nu hitvā priyo bhavati kiṃ nu hitvā na śocati kiṃ nu hitvārthavān bhavati kiṃ nu hitvā sukhī bhavet
english: The yaksha said: By giving up what does one become dear? By giving up what does one not grieve? By giving up what does one become wealthy? By giving up what does one become happy?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mānaṃ hitvā priyo bhavati krodhaṃ hitvā na śocati kāmaṃ hitvārthavān bhavati lobhaṃ hitvā sukhī bhavet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By giving up pride one becomes dear; by giving up anger one does not grieve; by giving up desire one becomes wealthy; by giving up greed one becomes happy.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca mṛtaḥ kathaṃ syāt puruṣaḥ kathaṃ rāṣṭraṃ mṛtaṃ bhavet śrāddhaṃ mṛtaṃ kathaṃ ca syāt kathaṃ yajño mṛto bhavet
english: The yaksha said: How is a man dead? How is a kingdom dead? How is a śrāddha offering dead? How is a sacrifice dead?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mṛto daridraḥ puruṣo mṛtaṃ rāṣṭram arājakam mṛtam aśrotriyaṃ śrāddhaṃ mṛto yajñas tv adakṣiṇaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: A poor man is dead; a kingdom without a king is dead; a śrāddha performed without a learned brahmin is dead; a sacrifice without a sacrificial fee is dead.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kā dik kim udakaṃ proktaṃ kim annaṃ pārtha kiṃ viṣam śrāddhasya kālam ākhyāhi tataḥ piba harasva ca
english: The yaksha said: What is the direction? What is called water? What is food, O Pārtha? What is poison? Tell me the proper time for a śrāddha — then drink and carry.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca santo dig jalam ākāśaṃ gaur annaṃ prārthanā viṣam śrāddhasya brāhmaṇaḥ kālaḥ kathaṃ vā yakṣa manyase
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The good are the direction; space is the water; the cow is food; supplication is poison; a brahmin is the proper time for a śrāddha — or how do you think, O yaksha?

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca vyākhyātā me tvayā praśnā yāthātathyaṃ paraṃtapa puruṣaṃ tv idānīm ākhyāhi yaś ca sarvadhanī naraḥ
english: The yaksha said: You have explained my questions truly, O scorcher of foes. Now tell me who is a man, and who is the person possessed of all wealth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca divaṃ spṛśati bhūmiṃ ca śabdaḥ puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ yāvat sa śabdo bhavati tāvat puruṣa ucyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The fame of righteous deeds touches both heaven and earth; for as long as that fame endures, so long is one called a man.

sanskrit: tulye priyāpriye yasya sukhaduḥkhe tathaiva ca atītānāgate cobhe sa vai sarvadhanī naraḥ
english: One to whom the pleasant and the unpleasant are equal, and likewise pleasure and pain, and who is indifferent to both past and future — that person truly possesses all wealth.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca vyākhyātaḥ puruṣo rājan yaś ca sarvadhanī naraḥ tasmāt tavaiko bhrātṝṇāṃ yam icchasi sa jīvatu
english: The yaksha said: You have defined what a man is, O king, and who the person of all wealth is. Therefore, let whichever one of your brothers you wish come back to life.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śyāmo ya eṣa raktākṣo bṛhacchāla ivodgataḥ vyūḍhorasko mahābāhur nakulo yakṣa jīvatu
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This one who is dark-complexioned, red-eyed, rising like a great śāla tree, broad-chested, and long-armed — let Nakula live, O yaksha.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca priyas te bhīmaseno 'yam arjuno vaḥ parāyaṇam sa kasmān nakulaṃ rājan sāpatnaṃ jīvam icchasi
english: The yaksha said: This Bhīmasena is dear to you, and Arjuna is your refuge. Then why, O king, do you wish the stepbrother Nakula to live?

sanskrit: yasya nāgasahasreṇa daśasaṃkhyena vai balam tulyaṃ taṃ bhīmam utsṛjya nakulaṃ jīvam icchasi
english: Bhīma's strength is equal to ten thousand elephants — leaving him aside, you wish Nakula to live?

sanskrit: tathainaṃ manujāḥ prāhur bhīmasenaṃ priyaṃ tava atha kenānubhāvena sāpatnaṃ jīvam icchasi
english: And people say Bhīmasena is dearest to you — then by what reasoning do you wish your stepbrother to live?

sanskrit: yasya bāhubalaṃ sarve pāṇḍavāḥ samupāśritāḥ arjunaṃ tam apāhāya nakulaṃ jīvam icchasi
english: All the Pāṇḍavas depend on Arjuna's arm-strength — leaving even Arjuna aside, you wish Nakula to live?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmaḥ paramārthāc ca me matam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ cikīrṣāmi nakulo yakṣa jīvatu
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Non-cruelty is the highest dharma — this is my conviction in the highest sense. I wish to practice non-cruelty; let Nakula live, O yaksha.

sanskrit: dharmaśīlaḥ sadā rājā iti māṃ mānavā viduḥ svadharmān na caliṣyāmi nakulo yakṣa jīvatu
english: People know me as a king ever devoted to dharma; I shall not swerve from my own duty. Let Nakula live, O yaksha.

sanskrit: yathā kuntī tathā mādrī viśeṣo nāsti me tayoḥ mātṛbhyāṃ samam icchāmi nakulo yakṣa jīvatu
english: As Kuntī is to me, so is Mādrī — I make no distinction between the two mothers. I wish to treat them equally. Let Nakula live, O yaksha.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca yasya te 'rthāc ca kāmāc ca ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paraṃ matam tasmāt te bhrātaraḥ sarve jīvantu bharatarṣabha
english: The yaksha said: Because for you non-cruelty is held higher than both artha and kama, therefore let all your brothers live, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te yakṣavacanād udatiṣṭhanta pāṇḍavāḥ kṣutpipāse ca sarveṣāṃ kṣaṇe tasmin vyagacchatām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then at the yaksha's word the Pāṇḍavas rose up, and instantly all their hunger and thirst departed.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sarasy ekena pādena tiṣṭhantam aparājitam pṛcchāmi ko bhavān devo na me yakṣo mato bhavān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I ask you, the unconquered one standing on one foot in the lake — who are you, O god? I do not take you for a yaksha.

sanskrit: vasūnāṃ vā bhavān eko rudrāṇām atha vā bhavān atha vā marutāṃ śreṣṭho vajrī vā tridaśeśvaraḥ
english: Are you one of the Vasus, or one of the Rudras, or the best of the Maruts, or the wielder of the thunderbolt, the lord of the thirty gods?

sanskrit: mama hi bhrātara ime sahasraśatayodhinaḥ na taṃ yogaṃ prapaśyāmi yena syur vinipātitāḥ
english: For these brothers of mine are warriors capable of fighting hundreds of thousands — I see no means by which they could have been struck down.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ prativibuddhānām indriyāṇy upalakṣaye sa bhavān suhṛd asmākam atha vā naḥ pitā bhavān
english: I observe that those who have awakened have their senses at ease. Are you our friend, or are you our father?

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca ahaṃ te janakas tāta dharmo mṛduparākrama tvāṃ didṛkṣur anuprāpto viddhi māṃ bharatarṣabha
english: The yaksha said: I am your father, dear child — Dharma himself, O gentle-yet-valiant one. I came here wishing to see you. Know me to be thus, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yaśaḥ satyaṃ damaḥ śaucam ārjavaṃ hrīr acāpalam dānaṃ tapo brahmacaryam ity etās tanavo mama
english: Fame, truth, self-restraint, purity, uprightness, modesty, steadiness, generosity, austerity, and chastity — these are my embodied forms.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā samatā śāntis tapaḥ śaucam amatsaraḥ dvārāṇy etāni me viddhi priyo hy asi sadā mama
english: Non-violence, equanimity, peace, austerity, purity, and freedom from envy — know these as my gates; for you are always dear to me.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā pañcasu rakto 'si diṣṭyā te ṣaṭpadī jitā dve pūrve madhyame dve ca dve cānte sāṃparāyike
english: By good fortune you are devoted to the five virtues; by good fortune you have conquered the six-fold path — two at the beginning, two in the middle, and two at the end relating to the other world.

sanskrit: dharmo 'ham asmi bhadraṃ te jijñāsus tvām ihāgataḥ ānṛśaṃsyena tuṣṭo 'smi varaṃ dāsyāmi te 'nagha
english: I am Dharma; good fortune to you. I came here to test you. I am pleased by your non-cruelty; I shall grant you a boon, O sinless one.

sanskrit: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva rājendra dātā hy asmi tavānagha ye hi me puruṣā bhaktā na teṣām asti durgatiḥ
english: Choose a boon, O best of kings, for I am the giver; O sinless one. Those persons who are devoted to me never come to an evil fate.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca araṇīsahitaṃ yasya mṛga ādāya gacchati tasyāgnayo na lupyeran prathamo 'stu varo mama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: A deer has carried off the fire-sticks of a brahmin — may his sacred fires not be lost. Let this be my first boon.

sanskrit: dharma uvāca araṇīsahitaṃ tasya brāhmaṇasya hṛtaṃ mayā mṛgaveṣeṇa kaunteya jijñāsārthaṃ tava prabho
english: Dharma said: It was I who took those fire-sticks from that brahmin in the form of a deer, O son of Kuntī, in order to test you, my lord.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dadānīty eva bhagavān uttaraṃ pratyapadyata anyaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varaṃ tvam amaropama
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The lord replied "I grant it" and said further: Choose another boon; good fortune to you, O one equal to the immortals.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca varṣāṇi dvādaśāraṇye trayodaśam upasthitam tatra no nābhijānīyur vasato manujāḥ kva cit
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: We have spent twelve years in the forest and the thirteenth is at hand — may no men anywhere recognise us while we dwell in that year.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dadānīty eva bhagavān uttaraṃ pratyapadyata bhūyaś cāśvāsayām āsa kaunteyaṃ satyavikramam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The lord again replied "I grant it" and further reassured the son of Kuntī, he of true valour.

sanskrit: yady api svena rūpeṇa cariṣyatha mahīm imām na vo vijñāsyate kaś cit triṣu lokeṣu bhārata
english: Even if you roam this earth in your own forms, no one in the three worlds will recognise you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: varṣaṃ trayodaśaṃ cedaṃ matprasādāt kurūdvahāḥ virāṭanagare gūḍhā avijñātāś cariṣyatha
english: By my grace, during this thirteenth year, O upholders of the Kuru lineage, you will roam in the city of Virāṭa concealed and unrecognised.

sanskrit: yad vaḥ saṃkalpitaṃ rūpaṃ manasā yasya yādṛśam tādṛśaṃ tādṛśaṃ sarve chandato dhārayiṣyatha
english: Whatever form each of you desires in mind, exactly that form will each of you bear according to your will.

sanskrit: araṇīsahitaṃ cedaṃ brāhmaṇāya prayacchata jijñāsārthaṃ mayā hy etad āhṛtaṃ mṛgarūpiṇā
english: Return these fire-sticks to the brahmin; for I took them in the form of a deer in order to test you.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ gṛhyatāṃ putra varam apratimaṃ mahat tvaṃ hi matprabhavo rājan viduraś ca mamāṃśabhāk
english: Take a third boon, my son — one that is matchless and great; for you spring from me, O king, and Vidura too has a share in me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca devadevo mayā dṛṣṭo bhavān sākṣāt sanātanaḥ yaṃ dadāsi varaṃ tuṣṭas taṃ grahīṣyāmy ahaṃ pitaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have seen you directly, O god of gods, the eternal one. Whatever boon you are pleased to give, that I shall accept, O father.

sanskrit: jayeyaṃ lobhamohau ca krodhaṃ cāhaṃ sadā vibho dāne tapasi satye ca mano me satataṃ bhavet
english: May I always conquer greed, delusion, and anger, O mighty lord, and may my mind be ever fixed on giving, austerity, and truth.

sanskrit: dharma uvāca upapanno guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ svabhāvenāsi pāṇḍava bhavān dharmaḥ punaś caiva yathoktaṃ te bhaviṣyati
english: Dharma said: You are by nature endowed with all virtues, O Pāṇḍava. You are dharma itself, and what you have asked shall come to pass as spoken.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvāntardadhe dharmo bhagavāṃl lokabhāvanaḥ sametāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva sukhasuptā manasvinaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Dharma the lord, nourisher of the worlds, disappeared. The assembled Pāṇḍavas, those high-minded ones, then slept peacefully.

sanskrit: abhyetya cāśramaṃ vīrāḥ sarva eva gataklamāḥ āraṇeyaṃ dadus tasmai brāhmaṇāya tapasvine
english: The heroes, all freed from fatigue, went to the hermitage and returned the fire-sticks to that brahmin ascetic.

sanskrit: idaṃ samutthānasamāgamaṃ mahat; pituś ca putrasya ca kīrtivardhanam paṭhan naraḥ syād vijitendriyo vaśī; saputrapautraḥ śatavarṣabhāg bhavet
english: This great account of the meeting between father and son, which enhances glory — a man who recites it shall have his senses conquered, be self-controlled, and enjoy a hundred years with sons and grandsons.

sanskrit: na cāpy adharme na suhṛdvibhedane; parasvahāre paradāramarśane kadaryabhāve na ramen manaḥ sadā; nṛṇāṃ sadākhyānam idaṃ vijānatām
english: His mind shall never take pleasure in unrighteousness, in sowing discord among friends, in taking another's property, in violating another's wife, or in meanness — for those who ever recite this account.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dharmeṇa te 'bhyanujñātāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ satyavikramāḥ ajñātavāsaṃ vatsyantaś channā varṣaṃ trayodaśam upopaviśya vidvāṃsaḥ sahitāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus authorised by Dharma, the Pāṇḍavas of true valour, intent on living in concealment for the thirteenth year, sat together — learned men, assembled, their vows sharpened.

sanskrit: ye tadbhaktā vasanti sma vanavāse tapasvinaḥ tān abruvan mahātmānaḥ śiṣṭāḥ prāñjalayas tadā abhyanujñāpayiṣyantas taṃ nivāsaṃ dhṛtavratāḥ
english: The great-souled ones, disciplined and firm in their vows, then addressed the ascetics who had been devoted to them during the forest life, with palms joined, seeking their leave for the impending residence.

sanskrit: viditaṃ bhavatāṃ sarvaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrair yathā vayam chadmanā hṛtarājyāś ca niḥsvāś ca bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ
english: It is known to you all how by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra we were stripped of our kingdom by deceit and reduced to poverty in many ways.

sanskrit: uṣitāś ca vane kṛcchraṃ yatra dvādaśa vatsarān ajñātavāsasamayaṃ śeṣaṃ varṣaṃ trayodaśam tad vatsyāmo vayaṃ channās tad anujñātum arhatha
english: We have lived in hardship in the forest for twelve years, and now the thirteenth year — the term of concealed residence — remains. We shall live it out in hiding; please grant us leave.

sanskrit: suyodhanaś ca duṣṭātmā karṇaś ca sahasaubalaḥ jānanto viṣamaṃ kuryur asmāsv atyantavairiṇaḥ yuktācārāś ca yuktāś ca paurasya svajanasya ca
english: The wicked-souled Suyodhana, Karṇa, and Śakuni together would do us mischief if they knew, for they are our utter enemies, ever watchful and in concert with the townspeople and our own kinsmen.

sanskrit: api nas tad bhaved bhūyo yad vayaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha samastāḥ sveṣu rāṣṭreṣu svarājyasthā bhavemahi
english: May it come to pass that we, together with the brahmins, assembled as one, be restored to our own kingdoms, established in sovereign rule.

sanskrit: ity uktvā duḥkhaśokārtaḥ śucir dharmasutas tadā saṃmūrchito 'bhavad rājā sāśrukaṇṭho yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having spoken thus, afflicted by sorrow and grief, the pure son of Dharma, King Yudhiṣṭhira, fainted, his throat choked with tears.

sanskrit: tam athāśvāsayan sarve brāhmaṇā bhrātṛbhiḥ saha atha dhaumyo 'bravīd vākyaṃ mahārthaṃ nṛpatiṃ tadā
english: Then all the brahmins along with his brothers consoled him, and Dhaumya spoke weighty words to the king.

sanskrit: rājan vidvān bhavān dāntaḥ satyasaṃdho jitendriyaḥ naivaṃvidhāḥ pramuhyanti narāḥ kasyāṃ cid āpadi
english: O king, you are learned, self-restrained, true to your pledges, and master of your senses — men of this kind do not lose heart in any adversity.

sanskrit: devair apy āpadaḥ prāptāś channaiś ca bahuśas tathā tatra tatra sapatnānāṃ nigrahārthaṃ mahātmabhiḥ
english: Even the gods have suffered adversities, and the great-souled ones have many times lived in concealment in various places for the purpose of subduing their enemies.

sanskrit: indreṇa niṣadhān prāpya giriprasthāśrame tadā channenoṣya kṛtaṃ karma dviṣatāṃ balanigrahe
english: Indra, reaching the Niṣāda lands and dwelling concealed in a mountain hermitage, accomplished the work of subduing the strength of enemies.

sanskrit: viṣṇunāśvaśiraḥ prāpya tathādityāṃ nivatsyatā garbhe vadhārthaṃ daityānām ajñātenoṣitaṃ ciram
english: Viṣṇu, taking the form of a horse-head and dwelling in Aditi's womb for a long time unrecognised, did so for the purpose of slaying the daityas.

sanskrit: prāpya vāmanarūpeṇa pracchannaṃ brahmarūpiṇā baler yathā hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ vikramais tac ca te śrutam
english: Taking the form of a dwarf, concealed in a brahmin's guise, he took the kingdom from Bali by his strides — that too you have heard.

sanskrit: aurveṇa vasatā channam ūrau brahmarṣiṇā tadā yatkṛtaṃ tāta lokeṣu tac ca sarvaṃ śrutaṃ tvayā
english: What the brahmin-sage Aurva accomplished while dwelling concealed in a thigh — all of that, dear child, you have heard.

sanskrit: pracchannaṃ cāpi dharmajña hariṇā vṛtranigrahe vajraṃ praviśya śakrasya yatkṛtaṃ tac ca te śrutam
english: And what Hari accomplished while concealed, entering Indra's thunderbolt for the subduing of Vṛtra, O knower of dharma — that too you have heard.

sanskrit: hutāśanena yac cāpaḥ praviśya channam āsatā vibudhānāṃ kṛtaṃ karma tac ca sarvaṃ śrutaṃ tvayā
english: And what Agni the fire-god accomplished for the gods while entering the waters and dwelling concealed — all of that you have heard.

sanskrit: evaṃ vivasvatā tāta channenottamatejasā nirdagdhāḥ śatravaḥ sarve vasatā bhuvi sarvaśaḥ
english: Thus by Vivasvat too, dear child, of supreme splendour dwelling concealed on the earth, all enemies everywhere were utterly consumed.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā vasatā cāpi gṛhe daśarathasya vai daśagrīvo hataś channaṃ saṃyuge bhīmakarmaṇā
english: And by Viṣṇu, dwelling in Daśaratha's house, the ten-necked one was slain, concealed and of terrible deeds in battle.

sanskrit: evam ete mahātmānaḥ pracchannās tatra tatra ha ajayañ śātravān yuddhe tathā tvam api jeṣyasi
english: Thus these great-souled ones, concealed here and there, conquered their enemies in battle — and so too shall you conquer.

sanskrit: tathā dhaumyena dharmajño vākyaiḥ saṃparitoṣitaḥ śāstrabuddhyā svabuddhyā ca na cacāla yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Thus the knower of dharma, fully consoled by Dhaumya's words, by the wisdom of the scriptures and by his own wisdom, Yudhiṣṭhira did not waver.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahābāhur bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ rājānaṃ balināṃ śreṣṭho girā saṃpariharṣayan
english: Then the long-armed Bhīmasena of great strength, the best among the strong, spoke to the king, cheering him with his words.

sanskrit: avekṣayā mahārāja tava gāṇḍīvadhanvanā dharmānugatayā buddhyā na kiṃ cit sāhasaṃ kṛtam
english: Out of deference to you, O great king, and by the dharma-guided wisdom of the Gāṇḍīva-bowman, nothing rash has been done.

sanskrit: sahadevo mayā nityaṃ nakulaś ca nivāritau śaktau vidhvaṃsane teṣāṃ śatrughnau bhīmavikramau
english: Sahadeva and Nakula were always restrained by me — though capable of destroying those enemies, those two destroyers of foes of terrible might.

sanskrit: na vayaṃ tat prahāsyāmo yasmin yokṣyati no bhavān bhavān vidhattāṃ tat sarvaṃ kṣipraṃ jeṣyāmahe parān
english: We shall not abandon that undertaking in which you engage us. Let your lordship arrange everything; we shall swiftly conquer the enemies.

sanskrit: ity ukte bhīmasenena brāhmaṇāḥ paramāśiṣaḥ prayujyāpṛcchya bharatān yathāsvān svān yayur gṛhān
english: When Bhīmasena had spoken thus, the brahmins pronounced supreme blessings, took their leave of the Bhāratas, and each departed to his own home.

sanskrit: sarve vedavido mukhyā yatayo munayas tathā āśīr uktvā yathānyāyaṃ punar darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: All the foremost knowers of the Vedas, the ascetics and sages, having pronounced blessings duly and wishing to see them again, departed.

sanskrit: saha dhaumyena vidvāṃsas tathā te pañca pāṇḍavāḥ utthāya prayayur vīrāḥ kṛṣṇām ādāya bhārata
english: Then those five wise Pāṇḍava heroes, together with Dhaumya and taking Kṛṣṇa along, rose and departed, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: krośamātram atikramya tasmād deśān nimittataḥ śvobhūte manujavyāghrāś channavāsārtham udyatāḥ
english: Having traveled only a krosa from that region due to a certain sign, those tigers among men, on the morrow, made themselves ready for the life of concealment.

sanskrit: pṛthakśāstravidaḥ sarve sarve mantraviśāradāḥ saṃdhivigrahakālajñā mantrāya samupāviśan
english: All were separately versed in the treatises, all were skilled in counsel, all knew the proper times for alliance and war — they sat together in council.
